item.title: php2shell CVEs, LiteLLM Supply-Chain Malware, and Vendor Bank-Change Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Oct 10:00 → 21 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

LiteLLM compromised again: infostealer and RAT found in version 1.107.0 — Must Read

LiteLLM version 1.107.0 and its corresponding Docker images were compromised to install an infostealer and persistent Python RAT that can steal credentials and execute attacker commands. Anyone who installed or ran the affected release should treat secrets as exposed, investigate affected hosts, and rotate credentials immediately.

  • LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised through malicious code injected into Python wheels published on PyPI, and its official Docker image for the same version was also affected.
  • The malicious package installed files that automatically ran whenever Python started, including an infostealer that collected credentials and secrets and a background program that could execute attacker-provided code.
  • The infostealer collected browser passwords, SSH keys, cloud credentials, environment variables, LiteLLM database contents, and other developer and CI/CD secrets, then sent the data to an attacker-controlled website.
  • The remote-access component checked every hour for code supplied by the attacker and ran it with the permissions of the affected Python process.
  • PyPI quarantined LiteLLM 1.107.0, but the article states that the compromised litellm/litellm:1.107.0 Docker image remained available on Docker Hub.

Technologies: proxy, package-registry, container-platform, source-control

Products: litellm, pypi, docker-hub, github, maturin

Vendors: litellm, pypi, docker, github, maturin

Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability — Must Read

Cloudflare automatically deployed WAF protections for all customers against the critical php2shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), which can enable PHP denial of service, data exposure, or remote code execution. Organizations should still urgently patch their PHP runtime and keep WAF protections enabled.

  • The php2shell vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affect PHP 5.4 and later and may allow denial of service, remote code execution, or data exposure through specially crafted HTTP traffic.
  • Cloudflare deployed WAF protections about nine hours before public disclosure, and customers using its free or paid WAF were protected by default beginning October 21 at 3:02 am UTC.
  • Cloudflare observed attack traffic targeting customers after the vulnerability leaked and saw attackers modify payloads in attempts to bypass protections.
  • Cloudflare introduced full transaction detection, which evaluates request and response signals from the same HTTP transaction and can block a matching origin response before it reaches the requester.
  • Cloudflare recommends that administrators apply the PHP vendor update while keeping WAF protections enabled, because updating application code or plugins alone does not fix the PHP runtime flaws.

Technologies: waf

Products: php, cloudflare-waf, cloudflare-managed-ruleset

Vendors: cloudflare, php-foundation, openai, wiz, quarkslab

The Hover Check Passed: Every Link Went to the Real Vendor — May Read

A vendor bank-change BEC email used a newly registered lookalike domain while embedding genuine vendor website and email links, so hover checks and URL scans appeared clean. The fraud was exposed by sender-domain scrutiny and contradictory, recently edited PDF metadata rather than any malicious link or payload.

  • A bank-change email came from mackaycomm[.]com, a lookalike domain registered 28 days before the message, rather than the genuine vendor’s domain.
  • The email’s signature links and email address visibly used the lookalike domain but directed recipients to the genuine vendor’s website and a real vendor employee, causing link scans to return clean results.
  • A JPMorgan Chase confirmation letter attached to the email displayed a 2026 date but had a 2025 source creation date and was modified on the morning the message was sent.
  • The two attached PDFs disagreed about the bank branch, the signer’s job title, and phone details, and the vendor-letterhead document was originally scanned in 2019 before being edited on the send date.
  • A human analyst classified the message as malicious and removed all four copies from recipient mailboxes, while a later automated re-analysis labeled it safe based on the clean links.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, google, jpmorgan-chase

How Tenable brought multi-language support to security detectors with agentic translation — Optional

Tenable replaced its costly translate-then-detect workflow with a multilingual security detection model trained using an agentic, label-preserving translation pipeline. The resulting Tenable One AI Exposure detectors support 10 validated languages with substantially lower latency and cost while matching or improving detection quality.

  • Tenable replaced its translate-then-detect approach with a single multilingual model that natively detects AI threats, harmful content, and policy risks in 10 validated languages.
  • The company used an agentic translation pipeline in which a frontier LLM creates label-aware translations, independent judges assess fluency and meaning preservation, and failed items are refined or handled by a controlled open-source model after refusals.
  • Tenable reports that native multilingual detection operates in tens of milliseconds, is roughly 20 to 800 times faster per item than the prior translation-based process, and uses less than 1 GB of memory versus 12 to 14 GB.
  • The multilingual model matched or exceeded translate-then-detect AI-threat detection on 9 of 10 languages and overall, and led on every language for the harmful-content detection evaluation described in the article.
  • Tenable states that its model may read and flag attacks in thousands of languages beyond the 10 it formally validated, but says that broader capability requires further testing before it can be relied upon.

Products: tenable-one-ai-exposure

Vendors: tenable

item.title: Critical Drupal and PHP RCE Flaws Amid Trusted-Service Phishing Abuse
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Oct 06:00 → 21 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

php2shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619): Frequently asked questions about critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities — Must Read

PHP is preparing emergency patches for two critical remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with early attacks reportedly emerging. Organizations should urgently update supported PHP 8.x releases when patches become available, as end-of-life branches may not receive fixes.

  • CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP vulnerabilities rated CVSSv4.0 9.2 by the PHP security team and publicly described as remote code execution flaws.
  • PHP scheduled an emergency security release for October 21, 2026 at 14:00 UTC, with expected fixes for PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
  • Cloudflare said it was seeing early attacks emerging and deployed WAF rules for known exploit paths, while describing those rules as a temporary stopgap.
  • End-of-life PHP versions from PHP 5.x through PHP 8.1.x are not expected to receive official fixes.
  • PHP core developers stated that patching or upgrading PHP is the only mitigation, and CERT-EU recommended considering isolating internet-facing applications where immediate patching is not feasible.

Technologies: waf

Products: php

Vendors: php-foundation, cloudflare, tenable

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-108097) Drupal Core Field UI Remote Code Execution — Should Read

Drupal has released patches for critical CVE-2026-108097 in the Field UI module, which can enable remote code execution when contributed or custom code routes request-controlled data into vulnerable render arrays. Update to the fixed core release for your branch immediately, or uninstall Field UI temporarily if patching is delayed.

  • CVE-2026-108097 is a critical remote code execution flaw in Drupal core's Field UI module, disclosed by Drupal as SA-CORE-2026-014 on 14 October 2026.
  • Drupal states that core alone is not directly exploitable; exploitation requires contributed or custom code that allows request-influenced data to reach the affected Field UI table render-array key.
  • Drupal released fixed versions 10.6.19, 11.3.19, and 11.4.10, while Drupal 12 pre-release users should move to 12.0.0-beta2 or later.
  • Organizations that cannot immediately update can uninstall the Field UI module as a workaround, according to Drupal.
  • Drupal 7 and unsupported older Drupal 10.x and 11.x branches do not receive a fix for this advisory and should be treated as migration work.

Technologies: cms

Products: drupal-core, field-ui, drupal-steward, cycognito-platform

Vendors: drupal, cycognito

Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers — Optional

Attackers are abusing legitimate transactional, registration, and mail-delivery systems to send attacker-controlled content in authenticated, trusted-looking emails. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC validate the sender infrastructure but cannot prove that reflected order details, support numbers, or nested bounce content are safe.

  • Cisco Talos observed attackers abusing more than 25 legitimate platforms during the past year, including collaboration, productivity, file-sharing, survey, payment, AI-related, retail, and email-delivery services.
  • Two campaigns used Staples and Dell order-notification workflows to send roughly 1,400 messages containing attacker-controlled helpline phone numbers inside transaction fields for unexpected high-value purchases.
  • The Staples and Dell messages passed sender-authentication checks because they originated from legitimate infrastructure, but those checks did not establish that the displayed order details or phone numbers were legitimate.
  • Attackers can use registration or subscription forms to place fraudulent text into user-controlled fields that trusted services later repeat in automated welcome, verification, or notification emails.
  • Delivery-status notifications can also carry phishing lures when returned messages or message fragments are included inside legitimate-looking failure reports, making recursive inspection of nested email content important.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-365, proton-mail, wetransfer

Vendors: cisco, staples, dell, microsoft, proton, wetransfer

item.title: Lazarus Operation FlashHole Targets South Korea; vlt Adds Agent Skills Management
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Oct 02:00 → 21 Oct 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

Operation FlashHole: Lazarus breaks security, defies control — Must Read

Kaspersky reports that Lazarus Group’s Operation FlashHole targeted South Korean organizations by abusing mandatory CrossWeb EX security software and tailored phishing sites to deliver a highly modular, largely memory-resident malware chain. The campaign combines updated TechHub, Cubridge, TouchShift, ClientHub, and LPEClient tooling with GitHub- and compromised-site-based C2 infrastructure for espionage and payload delivery.

  • Kaspersky identified Operation FlashHole as a Lazarus Group campaign targeting at least three South Korean organizations in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment sectors.
  • The campaign used tailored phishing links to GitHub Pages sites posing as a job résumé or interior design portfolio, with evidence suggesting the lure content included AI-generated material.
  • The infection chain abused the South Korean financial-security software CrossWeb EX and executed much of its malware chain in memory to reduce traces on disk.
  • The operation used updated and newly identified malware including TechHub, Cubridge, TouchHub, TouchShift, ClientHub, and LPEClient, with GitHub repositories and compromised South Korean websites used for command-and-control communications.
  • Kaspersky assessed with medium-to-high confidence that Operation FlashHole is the latest wave of the broader Cascade Hole campaign and is linked to Lazarus Group activity.

Technologies: operating-system, source-control, cloud-platform, object-storage, browser

Products: inisafe-crossweb-ex, windows, github-pages, github-api, dropbox, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, brave

Vendors: kaspersky, initech, microsoft, github, dropbox, google

vlt 1.5.0 Adds Agent Skills Management — May Read

vlt 1.5.0 adds opt-in agent-skill management, allowing developers to link coding-agent instructions from installed package dependencies and keep them synchronized with lockfile-pinned versions. It also uses Socket security data to exclude skills from packages flagged as malware or other security risks.

  • vlt 1.5.0 introduces the vlt skills command, which finds agent instruction folders in installed dependencies and links selected skills into directories used by coding agents.
  • Skill selections are saved as allow-skills in vlt.json, allowing subsequent installs, updates, and vlt ci to maintain the configured links.
  • By default, vlt links skills into .agents/skills and can also use existing agent-specific folders such as .claude/skills.
  • When no selection is saved, vlt skills link excludes packages flagged as malware by Socket’s high-confidence alerts.
  • pnpm 12.11.0 also added support for linking skills from approved direct dependencies, indicating that JavaScript package managers are adding management of coding-agent instructions.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: vlt, socket, pnpm, agent-browser, codex, cursor, github-copilot, gemini-cli, claude

Vendors: vlt, socket, pnpm, openai, github, google, anthropic, npm

item.title: Cloudflare Responds to Compromised eMudhra Intermediate Certificate Keys
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Oct 22:00 → 21 Oct 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know — Should Read

Eight compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate keys could enable forged certificates and TLS traffic interception for any domain, prompting Cloudflare to deploy mitigations and release updates for WARP/Cloudflare One and cloudflared. Customers should update affected software and trust stores, rebuild and restart applications as needed, and never disable certificate verification to bypass resulting errors.

  • Cloudflare learned at approximately 17:00 UTC on October 19, 2026, that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates had been compromised.
  • Because the compromised keys can be used to create forged certificates for any domain, attackers could impersonate servers and intercept or modify traffic.
  • Cloudflare released security updates for Cloudflare One Clients/WARP and Cloudflare Tunnel/cloudflared, and deployed mitigations across its CDN, Developer, and Zero Trust products.
  • Cloudflare said customers using Zero Trust Gateway with an up-to-date client are automatically protected, while some other customers may need to update software or trust configurations on systems they operate.
  • Cloudflare advises developers to update relevant dependencies, rebuild affected images, restart or redeploy applications where necessary, and not disable certificate verification to resolve errors.

Technologies: vpn, proxy, remote-access, browser

Products: cloudflare-one-client, warp, 1-1-1-1, cloudflare-tunnel, cloudflared, cloudflare-gateway, chrome, crlsets, upki

Vendors: cloudflare, emudhra, mozilla, ubuntu

item.title: Anthropic AI Worm Tests Expose IoT Replication Limits
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Oct 18:00 → 20 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

AI Tries (and Fails) to Worm Its Way into Your IoT Gadgets — Optional

Anthropic’s AI-worm experiments show that small models can be distributed across poorly secured IoT devices in lab conditions, but the article argues they do not demonstrate realistic autonomous self-replication. Existing security practices—strong authentication, segmentation, access controls, and behavior monitoring—remain the practical defense if such threats mature.

  • Anthropic described experiments in which a small AI model was distributed across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes and an open-weight model was used to locate and infect eight Google Cloud Platform nodes running an Android emulator.
  • Anthropic reported that current IoT hardware limited on-device performance to about one-third of a token per second and replication rates to days rather than rapid spread.
  • The article argues that the experiments omitted key real-world worm steps, including network enumeration, initial access, payload delivery, privilege escalation, authentication barriers, and bypassing security controls.
  • The second experiment relied on a script rather than autonomous, persistent self-replication, according to the article.
  • The article concludes that established measures such as behavior monitoring, access controls, activity constraints, and network and system security practices can help limit the damage of self-replicating AI programs if they become viable.

Technologies: cloud-platform, mobile-os, iot-device

Products: google-cloud-platform, android-tv, android-emulator

Vendors: anthropic, google

item.title: Doppelgänger Targets Israel as AI Reshapes Vulnerability Discovery and Online Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Oct 14:00 → 20 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Doppelgänger Russian Influence Campaign in Israel — Should Read

ClearSky reports that Russia-linked Doppelgänger operators revived an influence campaign targeting Israel, using fake Walla articles and X accounts to spread misleading narratives. The activity appears intended to erode trust, deepen social divisions, and potentially influence Israel’s October 2026 elections.

  • ClearSky identified renewed activity in Israel by the Russian influence campaign known as Doppelgänger, or “The Double.”
  • Doppelgänger creates fake copies of recognized news sites, using similar designs, logos, and layouts to appear legitimate.
  • The campaign spreads false and misleading messages based partly on real publications through fake social-media accounts, mainly on X.
  • ClearSky documented at least 76 fake articles published between May and October 2026 on walla[.]ist, a website impersonating Walla.
  • The campaign aims to advance Russian interests, weaken trust in Israeli institutions, deepen divisions in Israeli society, and pollute AI engines.

Vendors: clearsky

Rust 1.100 Will Add Dependency Cooldowns to Cargo — Should Read

Rust 1.100 will add an opt-in Cargo dependency cooldown that blocks newly published crate versions for a configurable period, helping limit exposure to malicious supply-chain releases. The protection is not enabled by default, so teams must configure a minimum publish age themselves.

  • Rust 1.100, scheduled for November 12, will add stable support for Cargo’s configurable minimum publish age, although the setting remains disabled by default.
  • With a configured minimum publish age, Cargo excludes dependency releases that are newer than the specified waiting period and fails resolution if no eligible version satisfies the project’s requirements.
  • Compromised releases of arrayref, internment, and append-only-vec were available on crates.io for 86, 90, and 107 minutes, respectively, before removal in August.
  • Cargo preserves dependency versions already recorded in Cargo.lock even when they are younger than the configured minimum age.
  • The stabilized implementation does not apply the publish-age check to cargo install, Git dependencies, local path dependencies, or registries without publication timestamp metadata.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: cargo, crates-io

Vendors: rust-project, crates-io

There's only so much code: the rise in vulnerability numbers — Optional

AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is driving a sharp rise in disclosed flaws in legacy software, but most are not being exploited in the wild. Defenders should prioritize vulnerabilities that are demonstrably exploitable in their environments while strengthening layered mitigations and patching processes.

  • Frontier AI models, including Mythos, are rapidly finding previously undiscovered weaknesses in decades-old, widely used software, contributing to 1,415 Microsoft vulnerability advisories in October after 975 in September.
  • The article reports that only three of Microsoft’s 975 September vulnerability advisories had detected in-the-wild exploitation, while Known Exploited Vulnerabilities increased 37% year over year compared with a 105% increase in published CVEs.
  • Open-source projects are being flooded with vulnerability reports, placing pressure on maintainers and challenging the traditional 90-day coordinated disclosure model.
  • The article suggests AI-assisted discovery may eventually level off as the backlog of historical code is reviewed and new software is checked with AI before release.
  • The article recommends that organizations prioritize flaws with high exploitability in their own environments, patch promptly, use interim mitigations such as LiveProtect, and deploy layered behavioral and intrusion-prevention protections.

Technologies: ids-ips

Products: mythos, log4j, microsoft-active-protections-program, liveprotect, snort, snortml

Vendors: microsoft, cisco, apache-software-foundation

The Risk of AI-Powered Antidetect Browsers in Online Fraud and Influence Operations — Optional

AI-enabled antidetect browsers such as Kameleo, AdsPower, and MultiLogin let operators mask device identities, automate thousands of accounts, and evade platform defenses, enabling scalable fraud, account takeover, scraping, and coordinated influence campaigns. Their combination of fingerprint spoofing, residential proxies, cookie injection, account warming, and LLM-driven automation lowers the barrier for sophisticated abuse.

  • Antidetect browsers such as Kameleo, AdsPower, and MultiLogin create isolated browser profiles with fabricated device fingerprints, allowing operators to manage many accounts while attempting to evade platform detection.
  • The article documents criminal uses including account takeover through stolen session cookies, card testing with stolen payment credentials, fraudulent loan applications, and bulk creation of accounts for advertising fraud.
  • AdsPower provides automation features, including an RPA marketplace, account warming, and a Model Context Protocol server that can connect large language model workflows to browser profiles for automated content distribution.
  • Kameleo supports WebRTC suppression and cookie injection, which can insert an already authenticated session into a browser profile without a new login event.
  • The article argues that the combination of identity spoofing, residential proxies, automated account activity, scraping, and AI-generated content lowers the barrier for large-scale fraud and coordinated inauthentic influence operations.

Technologies: browser, proxy

Products: kameleo, adspower, multilogin, cookie-robot

Vendors: kameleo, adspower, multilogin, meta, cloudflare, datadome

PwC’s 2027 Global Digital Trust Insights survey of 3,934 business and technology leaders across 71 countries examines how organizations are managing cyber risk amid rapid AI advances, geopolitical volatility, and increasingly interconnected systems.

Advanced Attacks on Embedded Gen AI Tools and Gen AI Apps – What to Watch For — Optional

Healthcare organizations embedding generative AI into patient-facing apps and workflows should address security and compliance risks to avoid exposing patient data and damaging trust.

  • Digitized patient interactions and generative AI workflows can improve efficiency.
  • Healthcare organizations need to plan carefully to meet security and compliance needs when using these technologies.

Rust 1.100 Will Add Dependency Cooldowns to Cargo — Should Read

Rust 1.100 will let teams configure Cargo to avoid dependency releases published too recently, giving maintainers time to detect and remove malicious crates before automated updates adopt them. The protection is opt-in, defaults to no delay, and can be overridden for urgent updates.

  • Rust 1.100, scheduled for November 12, will add stable Cargo support for a configurable minimum age before newly published dependencies can be selected.
  • The feature is opt-in: Cargo’s default minimum publish age remains zero unless teams configure a delay such as seven days.

Three Angry Hotel Guests, Two Hijacked Mailboxes, One Script — May Read

A phishing campaign used hijacked institutional email accounts with valid SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication to send fake hotel guest complaints containing Google-hosted evidence links. The campaign shows that trusted sender authentication cannot detect account takeover, so organizations must verify grievance claims internally before opening links.

  • A UK luxury hotel received three phishing emails over ten days that used fake guest complaints about an alleged assault or charges for bookings that never confirmed.
  • The messages were sent from hijacked accounts at an Asian business association and a Latin American government ministry, using those institutions' legitimate authenticated mail systems.
  • The emails passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks at the hotel’s inbound gateway, illustrating that email authentication can validate a sending domain without proving the legitimate account holder sent the message.
  • All three messages used a shared client-generated Message-ID structure that linked the two compromised institutions to the same sending script.
  • The lures directed recipients to Google share-link URLs supposedly containing screenshots or video, although no attachments or payloads were observed.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: adaptive-ai, microsoft-365, google-share

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, google

The Risk of AI-Powered Antidetect Browsers in Online Fraud and Influence Operations — May Read

AI-integrated antidetect browsers such as Kameleo, AdsPower, and MultiLogin let small operators run large networks of seemingly distinct online identities, enabling account takeover, fraud, scraping, and coordinated influence campaigns while evading conventional platform detection. The report urges platforms and defenders to focus on infrastructure-level signals such as proxy use, fingerprint spoofing, and cookie-injection anomalies.

  • Antidetect browsers such as Kameleo, AdsPower, and MultiLogin create isolated browser profiles with fabricated device signals, allowing a single operator to manage many accounts while reducing platform detection.
  • The report describes criminal uses including taking over accounts through stolen session cookies, testing stolen payment cards, submitting fraudulent loan applications, and creating artificial accounts for advertising fraud.
  • AdsPower offers automation features, pre-built workflows, account warming, and a Model Context Protocol server that can connect AI-generated content to browser profiles for automated distribution.
  • Kameleo supports session-cookie injection and controls intended to prevent WebRTC from exposing a user’s real IP address, while MultiLogin offers automated browser profiles and cloud-hosted mobile-device profiles.
  • The article recommends that platforms and defenders focus on infrastructure-level signals, including residential proxy activity, WebRTC suppression, unusual cookie-injection sequences, and browser fingerprint consistency over time.

Technologies: browser

Products: kameleo, adspower, multilogin

Vendors: kameleo, adspower, multilogin

The journey of a paper unicorn: adventures inside a modern warehouse — Optional

Modern warehouses are tightly interconnected IT, OT, wireless, and physical environments where compromise of devices or the warehouse management system can disrupt operations, corrupt inventory, enable unauthorized shipments, and potentially affect safety. Defending them requires coordinated segmentation, zero-trust access, secure device and application management, wireless and physical controls, and regular security assessments.

  • Modern warehouses combine web applications, wireless networks, handheld terminals, printers, automation equipment, and building systems, with the warehouse management system coordinating all eight main fulfillment stages.

item.content:encoded:

Popular WordPress SEO Plugin Rank Math PRO Hijacked to Deliver Self-Restoring Backdoor — Must Read

Rank Math PRO builds downloaded or updated between October 15 and 16 were backdoored, potentially giving attackers persistent access to activated WordPress sites. Affected users should treat sites as compromised, restore from a pre-incident backup where possible, rotate all credentials, and install the clean 3.0.124 release only after remediation.

  • Rank Math PRO copies downloaded from rankmath.com or installed through updates between 20:02 UTC on October 15 and 07:12 UTC on October 16 contained malware.
  • Sites that installed and activated an affected copy should be treated as compromised because the malware can recreate a hidden backdoor when someone visits the site.
  • Rank Math released clean version 3.0.124, but installing it does not remove administrator accounts, scheduled tasks, or other malicious files that may already have been placed on a server.
  • Rank Math recommends restoring a backup from before October 15 where possible; otherwise, owners should first delete the entire Rank Math PRO folder, remove specified database entries, and block outgoing connections to rank1cdn.com.
  • Wordfence assigned the incident CVE-2026-111862 and rated it 9.8 out of 10.

Technologies: cms

Products: rank-math-seo-pro, wordpress

Vendors: rank-math, group-one, wordfence, patchstack, wordpress

OpenCode hack exposes API keys amid AI distillation attacks — Should Read

OpenCode says a large-scale AI model-distillation attack exposed external-provider API keys for 1.4% of its Console users, leading to unauthorized cloud charges and some suspended Google Cloud projects. Affected users have been notified and should rotate linked Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google API credentials.

  • OpenCode reported that a large-scale model-distillation attack exposed stored external-provider API keys for 1.4% of OpenCode Console users.
  • The affected users were those who had linked external providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, and OpenCode said it notified them by email.
  • OpenCode said the earliest possible exposure of users' keys was October 17, 2026, at 00:30 UTC, and that it found no indication that data was exposed.
  • Some affected users reported unauthorized API charges ranging from several hundred dollars to as much as $1,700, while others said Google suspended their projects for suspected hijacked-resource activity.
  • OpenCode co-founder Dax Raad said attackers targeted the company’s systems for at least 48 hours using AI agents, and the situation stabilized after OpenCode used OpenAI’s Daybreak cybersecurity model for defensive work.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: opencode-console, google-cloud, daybreak

Vendors: opencode, anthropic, openai, google

Ahold Delhaize confirms 'malicious actions' behind cyber outages affecting grocery brands — Should Read

Ahold Delhaize confirmed that malicious actors caused cyber outages affecting online grocery services across its U.S. and European brands, while physical stores remained open. The company is restoring systems in phases and says it has not yet found evidence of stolen sensitive data.

  • Ahold Delhaize confirmed that malicious actors caused the suspicious activity detected in its IT systems and filed a police report in the Netherlands.
  • The incident disrupted online services in the United States, the Netherlands, and Belgium, while stores remained open.
  • Ahold Delhaize said it had no evidence that sensitive customer, employee, or partner data was stolen, but its investigation remains ongoing.
  • Online shopping at U.S. brands including Food Lion and Stop & Shop was not yet functional, while Dutch websites and apps had returned and Albert Heijn home deliveries were expected to resume Friday.
  • The company said it notified Dutch cybersecurity authorities within 24 hours of detecting the incident and was restoring services in phases.

Russian social media giant VK faces disruptions after data center drone strike — Should Read

A Ukrainian FP-1 drone strike reportedly damaged a key VK data center near St. Petersburg, coinciding with widespread disruptions to VKontakte and its music services despite VK's claim that operations remained normal. The incident is part of escalating reciprocal attacks on Russian and Ukrainian data-center infrastructure.

  • A Ukrainian drone strike targeted a VK data center in Russia's Leningrad region overnight on October 18, according to VK and Ukrainian drone manufacturer Fire Point.
  • Users reported problems accessing VKontakte and VK's music service, including loading feeds, playing music, logging in, sending messages, and uploading photos and videos.
  • VK said its services remained available as usual and did not disclose the extent of any damage, while monitoring services recorded thousands of outage reports and NetBlocks reported VK connectivity fell to 56% of normal levels.
  • Fire Point said its FP-1 drones struck several regional targets including the VK facility, which it described as a key data center housing more than 20,000 servers in 640 racks based on previously published figures.
  • The reported disruptions occurred amid repeated Russian and Ukrainian attacks on data centers, including reported attacks on Yandex and Sberbank facilities in Russia and Datagroup and other facilities in Ukraine.

item.content:encoded:
Window: 19 Oct 10:00 → 19 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities — Must Read

F5 released urgent patches for three critical NGINX vulnerabilities that can cause denial-of-service and potentially remote code execution in non-default configurations. Organizations using affected NGINX products should patch promptly or apply the specified mitigations until updates can be installed.

  • F5 released out-of-band patches for three critical NGINX vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479.
  • The flaws can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial-of-service conditions or potentially execute code on NGINX systems using non-default configurations.
  • Affected products include NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source, NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Gateway Fabric, and NGINX Instance Manager.
  • F5 provided temporary mitigations, including avoiding certain alias and request filename settings, disabling asynchronous file I/O or server-side includes, and using named rather than unnamed captures.
  • F5 has not identified these vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild, but CISA has listed eight F5 vulnerabilities as actively exploited since November 2021.

Technologies: web-server, container-platform

Products: nginx, nginx-plus, nginx-open-source, nginx-ingress-controller, nginx-gateway-fabric, nginx-instance-manager

Vendors: f5

GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories — Should Read

GhostAction operators are phishing GitHub maintainers and using a fake font file plus VS Code auto-run tasks to steal developer credentials and persist on machines, affecting at least 94 repositories. The campaign bypasses GitHub Actions protections by targeting developers directly and harvesting reusable OAuth tokens, cloud keys, package-registry tokens, SSH keys, and AI-provider credentials.

  • GhostAction operators registered my-github.com and used it to send phishing emails impersonating GitHub security alerts to open-source maintainers.
  • The phishing site captured GitHub passwords and two-factor authentication codes, then silently approved an OAuth application with repository, workflow, and organization-read permissions.
  • Attackers added VS Code tasks configured to run when a folder opens and disguised a credential stealer as public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2.
  • The stealer targets AWS keys, PyPI and npm tokens, GitHub credentials, Kubernetes credentials, SSH private keys, and Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini credentials, then installs a cron job that runs attacker-supplied code every five minutes.
  • OpenSourceMalware identified the second-stage component in 94 compromised repositories belonging to 66 owners.

Technologies: source-control, ci-cd, iam

Products: github, github-actions, visual-studio-code

Vendors: github, microsoft

Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses npm Packages to Spread Malware and Hijack AI Agent Traffic — Should Read

A fake Web3 accelerator, tracked as REF8801, used malicious npm packages posing as AI and security tools to install Windows stealers and the macOS CloudSyncD backdoor. The packages also fabricated audit results and could redirect OpenRouter AI-agent traffic to attacker-controlled services, exposing prompts, code, and tool outputs.

  • A fake Web3 venture accelerator called Apex Accelerator, tracked as REF8801, distributed malicious npm packages that claimed to provide AI assistance and security auditing tools for cryptocurrency founders.
  • The @apexacc/cli and @apexacc/audit packages delivered a custom Windows information stealer and the macOS CloudSyncD backdoor instead of their advertised functionality.
  • On Windows, the malware collected system and browser data, wallet and application data, screenshots, Wi-Fi profile names, and other information before sending collected data through Telegram.
  • On macOS, CloudSyncD used a fake authorization prompt to request the victim's system password, then used elevated access to collect device details and obtain further instructions from an external server.
  • The packages could redirect OpenRouter AI-agent requests through attacker-controlled services and register an attacker-controlled MCP server, exposing prompts, conversation history, code snippets, and tool outputs.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, operating-system, browser

Products: npm, github, claude, gemini, openrouter, windows, macos, google-chrome

Vendors: anthropic, google, github, microsoft, apple, openrouter, elastic

Hackers steal customer data from major Russian hosting provider FirstVDS — Should Read

FirstVDS says attackers exploited a flaw in ISPsystem’s VMmanager 6 to silently copy sensitive customer data, including passwords, cloud credentials and cryptocurrency wallets, from some virtual servers. Affected customers were urged to rotate credentials while the provider restricts the vulnerable management system pending further fixes.

  • FirstVDS said attackers exploited a vulnerability in ISPsystem’s VMmanager 6 platform to access data from part of its infrastructure.
  • The attackers deployed software that copied customer data, including passwords, cloud-service credentials, configuration files and cryptocurrency wallets, to a server they controlled.
  • The company said the attackers mounted affected virtual-server disks in read-only mode, allowing data to be copied without altering files or disrupting normal operation.
  • FirstVDS urged customers who received breach notifications to assume their stored data was stolen and to change passwords and access credentials.
  • ISPsystem released several patches after the breach, but FirstVDS said the vulnerability was not yet fully fixed and external access to the management system remained disabled.

Technologies: hypervisor, cloud-platform

Products: vmmanager-6

Vendors: firstvds, ispsystem

The Foxit eSign Email That Erased Foxit — Should Read

Attackers abused authenticated Foxit eSign notifications to deliver a Binance callback-phishing lure, using CSS to hide Foxit’s table-based email content while leaving their own tableless HTML visible. The case shows that valid SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks do not prevent SaaS-platform abuse, and phone numbers should be treated as phishing payloads.

  • A fully authenticated Foxit eSign notification delivered a Binance-themed phone-change alert to four mailboxes at a US investment firm on January 25, 2026.
  • The email contained CSS that hid tables, rows, cells, and the button container, causing Foxit’s table-based branding and review-and-sign content to disappear in clients that honored the stylesheet.
  • The visible attacker content was built with divs and CSS grid rather than tables, and it instructed recipients to call +1 800-344-4914 to cancel an alleged phone-number change.
  • SPF, DKIM with d=foxitsign.com, and DMARC passed, while Microsoft EOP assigned the message an SCL 1 non-spam score and delivered it to the inbox.
  • IRONSCALES quarantined all four copies after labeling them as a first-time sender, Credential Theft, and VIP Recipient, and a human analyst resolved the incident as malicious.

Technologies: email-security

Products: foxit-esign, sendgrid, microsoft-eop, themis

Microsoft says it has fixed a classic Outlook bug that caused Copilot buttons to disappear when required account information could not be retrieved from users’ Outlook profiles. Users still affected can enable “Show Apps in Outlook,” create a new profile, or use new Outlook or Outlook on the web.

  • Microsoft says it resolved a classic Outlook issue that caused Copilot Chat and Copilot buttons to disappear for some Windows users.
  • The issue was caused by a bug that prevented Outlook from retrieving some required account information from a user’s Outlook profile.
  • Affected users could find the Copilot button missing above the ribbon or from the left app bar, while Copilot could remain available through Outlook on the web or the standalone Copilot experience.
  • Microsoft recommends using its Copilot troubleshooting guidance because missing Copilot buttons can also result from licensing, Microsoft 365 configuration, update channel, privacy settings, or other environmental factors.
  • Users still affected can enable the “Show Apps in Outlook” setting, create a new Outlook profile, or use the new Outlook client or Outlook Web Access.

The article promotes Cloudflare Access, Tunnel, and related controls as a defense-in-depth approach for Citrix desktop gateways and other public authentication services.

  • Citrix reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, including an unauthenticated command-execution flaw in default configurations.
  • Citrix released software updates for the flaws, and Cloudflare issued an emergency WAF rule for CVE-2026-88771 on October 1.
  • The article recommends putting Internet-facing authentication services behind an independent access policy so unauthenticated attackers cannot reach the gateway server.
  • It states that direct access to an origin IP address or alternate hostname can bypass access controls, so organizations should use Cloudflare Tunnel or restrict and authenticate origin connections.
  • The article notes that protecting the web authentication path does not automatically protect other gateway services, including DTLS-enabled listeners, which require their own exposure review and updates.

Technologies: load-balancer, remote-access, waf, iam, proxy

Products: citrix-netscaler-adc, citrix-netscaler-gateway, cloudflare-access, cloudflare-waf, cloudflare-tunnel, cloudflare-one-client, cloudflare-browser-isolation, cloudflare-browser-based-rdp, authenticated-origin-pulls, dedicated-cdn-egress-ips

Vendors: citrix, cloudflare

From Email-to-Case to the Boardroom: How Inherited Agents Break Governance Built for Software — Optional

The article argues that AI agents embedded in enterprise platforms such as Salesforce can be exposed through ordinary application workflows like Email-to-Case, making governance dependent on continuous discovery, configuration visibility, ownership, and runtime controls rather than policies alone.

  • Salesforce Agentforce can be connected through Flow, Email-to-Case, and Web-to-Case so that an inbound public message becomes a case record, is passed into an agent prompt, and may result in an outbound reply.
  • The article states that this Agentforce chain is a configuration rather than an exploit, and that its risk depends on application settings such as intake features, triggers, guest-user access, automation, and the underlying model version.
  • The City-Forum campaign is described as an active worldwide data-theft operation targeting Salesforce and ServiceNow instances since March 2025.
  • The article argues that effective agent governance requires continuous discovery, configuration assessment, named ownership, usage visibility, access controls, and live monitoring rather than policies and committees alone.
  • The article cites potential EU AI Act penalties of up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited practices, and up to €15 million or 3% for other violations.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: salesforce-agentforce, email-to-case, web-to-case, reco

Vendors: salesforce, servicenow, reco, owasp

Unmasking the robots: Why it’s critical to discover AI agent identities and how Tenable helps you secure them — Optional

Tenable has added Microsoft Entra Agent ID discovery to Tenable One Cloud Exposure, helping organizations inventory AI agent identities and identify associated cloud security risks. The article urges organizations to avoid assigning human or overprivileged service accounts to AI agents and instead use dedicated agent identity models.

  • AI agents make runtime decisions with large language models, interact with external tools and data sources, and adapt their actions, making their normal behavior difficult for security teams to define.
  • The article argues that organizations should not use human identities or overly privileged service accounts for vendor-deployed AI agents, and should instead require dedicated identity models such as Microsoft Entra Agent ID.
  • Microsoft Entra Agent ID uses a four-object model consisting of agent identity blueprints, agent identity blueprint principals, agent identities, and optional agent users.
  • Tenable announced that Tenable One Cloud Exposure now brings Microsoft Entra agentic AI identities into its unified asset and identity inventory.
  • The article says that native identity-management tools provide only basic information about AI agent identities and may leave security teams without sufficient context about their security flaws or attack-surface exposure.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, cloud-platform

Products: tenable-one-cloud-exposure, microsoft-entra-agent-id, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-copilot, microsoft-foundry

Vendors: tenable, microsoft

Drata and Aikido: audit-ready pentesting, built into your compliance workflow — Optional

Drata is offering new customers up to $4,000 in Aikido AI Pentest credits, with verified findings, auditor-ready reports, six months of retesting, and direct synchronization of evidence into Drata compliance workflows.

  • Drata and Aikido have integrated Aikido security testing evidence and findings into Drata’s compliance workflows for controls including SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA, and HIPAA.
  • New Drata customers on Foundation, Advanced, or Enterprise plans can claim up to $4,000 in Aikido AI Pentest credits, redeemable within the first three months of their Drata plan start date or for deals currently in progress.
  • Aikido states that its pentesting agents test applications, APIs, and supporting infrastructure, and that a separate agent re-exploits reported findings before they are included in the final report.
  • The offer includes six months of unlimited retesting so customers can verify fixes after they are deployed.
  • The article cites a survey in which 76% of leaders said they deploy significant production changes weekly or faster, while 21% said they validate security on every release.

Products: drata, aikido-ai-pentest

Vendors: drata, aikido, doyensec, xbow

item.title: Exchange Update Failures, Broadcom Router RCE, and OpenCode API Key Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 19 Oct 06:00 → 19 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers — Should Read

An unpatched flaw in Broadcom’s WPS implementation lets attackers within Wi‑Fi range send crafted setup frames and execute code as root on affected routers without knowing the network password. Millions of older and newer Broadcom-based devices may be exposed, with replacement often the only practical mitigation for unsupported models.

  • Researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed that a flaw in Broadcom’s Wi-Fi Protected Setup software can allow an attacker within radio range to run code as root on affected routers without a Wi-Fi password or pairing step.
  • Kaiser demonstrated the flaw against Belgian provider gateways, reading the Wi-Fi password from an Orange Belgium Askey TCG3000 and opening a Wi-Fi-carried reverse shell on a Proximus Sagemcom BBOX3V+.
  • The vulnerable code affects older eCos-based Broadcom BCM3380, BCM3383, and BCM33834 chips as well as newer Linux-based BCM3390, BCM65xx, and BCM68xx families, potentially affecting millions of devices.
  • Kaiser says older eCos-based devices have no usable fix and may remain permanently vulnerable, while newer models could be fixed if manufacturers move to hostapd Wi-Fi software.
  • No CVE has been assigned and no patch has been deployed for the affected routers; Kaiser provides YARA rules and a live-access-point checking script as triage tools.

Technologies: router, iot-device

Products: bcm3380, bcm3383, bcm33834, bcm3390, bcm65xx, bcm68xx, tcg3000, bbox3v-plus, hostapd

Vendors: broadcom, askey, sagemcom

Microsoft: October Windows Server updates break Exchange sign-in, mail flow — Should Read

Microsoft says October 2026 Windows Server security updates can disrupt Outlook on the web sign-ins and mail delivery on some on-premises Exchange servers due to a new Endpoint Mapper memory limit. A temporary registry change raising the Endpoint Lookup call cap can mitigate the issue while Microsoft develops a fix.

  • Microsoft confirmed that October 2026 Windows Server security updates can cause Outlook on the web sign-in and mail delivery problems on some on-premises Exchange Server systems running Windows Server 2019 or later.
  • Affected users may be unable to access email, messages sent from Outlook may remain in the Outbox, and Exchange may have trouble accessing mailboxes during mailbox replication.
  • Microsoft said the update introduced a default limit of 512 simultaneous Endpoint Lookup calls, which may be insufficient for heavily loaded Exchange Server workloads.
  • Microsoft provided a temporary workaround that raises the Endpoint Mapper limit through the EpmapSavedContextCap registry value and requires rebooting the Exchange Server.
  • Microsoft said the issue is unrelated to October 2026 Exchange Server security updates and advised customers not to uninstall those updates.

Technologies: operating-system, email-security

Products: exchange-server, outlook-on-the-web, windows-server-2019, windows-server-2025

Vendors: microsoft

OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys — Should Read

OpenCode says an intruder accessed a legacy Console system, potentially exposing OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys stored by 1.4% of Console users. Affected users should immediately revoke and replace provider keys and review their accounts for unauthorized usage.

  • OpenCode said an intruder accessed a legacy system connected to its optional Console service on the night of October 16, potentially exposing third-party AI provider keys saved there.
  • OpenCode said 1.4% of Console users were affected, all of whom had linked an outside provider, and it emailed them on October 17 to revoke and replace their keys.
  • The incident involved keys stored in OpenCode Console, while keys added locally to OpenCode’s command-line and desktop applications remain in a SQLite database on the user’s machine.
  • OpenCode advised affected users to review provider usage and billing for unauthorized requests, and some users reported charges they said they did not make.
  • OpenCode described the incident as ongoing and related to a large-scale model-distillation campaign, but did not disclose how the legacy system was accessed or whether any keys were copied or used.

Technologies: api-gateway, database

Products: opencode-console, opencode-cli, opencode-desktop, sqlite

Vendors: opencode, openai, anthropic, google

Proactively Defending Financial Institutions Against North Korean Remote IT Workers — Optional

North Korean operatives use legitimate or rented identities and domestic residential connections to secure remote IT jobs, allowing them to evade standard KYC and AML checks while routing salary payments back to North Korea. Financial institutions should analyze connection origins, payment-routing changes, and hiring anomalies before onboarding.

  • Silent Push identified a North Korean recruiting scheme on Discord in which a recruiter offered U.S., European Union, and Latin American citizens 35% of a salary to provide their identity and appear on job applications.
  • The remaining 65% of the salary is sent to the North Korean worker through cryptocurrency, wire transfers, or third-party payment processors.
  • The scheme can pass document-based KYC and AML checks because the identity is legitimate and the connection appears to come from a clean domestic residential IP address.
  • The operator may be located upstream of the residential address through a residential proxy or a KVM-over-IP relay in a laptop farm.
  • The report recommends that financial institutions examine where an applicant's connection begins, watch for early requests to redirect salary to an EMI or third-party account, and coordinate information sharing between HR and cybersecurity teams.

Technologies: proxy, remote-access

Vendors: silent-push
